17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans — 2119-29 West Grand Avenue, Chicago, IL
Proposed Zoning: §_B3-5 Community Shopping District
Lot Area: 13,125 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to develop the subject property with a new five-
story mixed-use building containing two (2) retail spaces at grade and forty-
eight (48) dwelling units above. One of the retail units will contain
approximately 2,640 sq. ft. of floor area and the second retail unit will
contain approximately 2,775 sq. ft. of floor area. The proposed building will
measure approximately 57 fi.-5 in. in height (67 ft.-8 in. measured to the
roof access room). The subject property is a Transit Served Location and
will be supported by thirty-four (34) off-street parking spaces. The subject
lot is a through lot with two (2) street frontages (West Grand Avenue to the
north and West Ferdinand Street to the south). Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-0303-
D optional Administrative Adjustment and Variation and pursuant to Secs.
17-13-1003-EE, 17-13-1003-P, Q, and R, and 17-13-1101-B of the Chicago
Zoning Ordinance, the Applicant is seeking to increase the residential off-
street parking ratio from 50% (24 parking spaces) to 70.83% (34 parking
spaces), to not comply with the TSL design guidelines on the lot’s West
Ferdinand Street frontage, reduce the front setback on the subject lot’s West
Ferdinand Street frontage for floors containing residential units from 30 feet
to 2 ft.-2 in., and is seeking all zoning relief, as needed and as allowed by
the Chicago Zoning Code, for the attached plans.

(A) — The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 57,942 square feet (4.415 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 273.43 square feet per D.U.
(48 residential units)

© The amount of off-street parking: 34 parking spaces total

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location based on its
proximity to Western Avenue Metra Train station. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-
EE, the Applicant is seeking to increase the off-street parking ratio from 50% (24
parking spaces) to 70.83% (34 parking spaces).

(D) Setbacks:
a. Front Setback from West Grand Avenue: zero
Front Setback from West Ferdinand Street; 2 feet-2 inches
b. Side Setbacks:
East Side: 2 feet-2 inches
West Side: 2 feet-2 inches

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 2,119 linear feet of the Westen Avenue Metra
train station. The proposed mixed-use building containing two (2) retail/commercial spaces
at grade and forty-eight (48) residential units above will be supported by thirty-four (34)
off-street parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to
permit an increase in the residential off-street parking ratio from 50% (24 parking spaces)
to 70.83% (34 parking spaces).

2. The Applicant is seeking relief from the requirements of Sec. 17-4-0504 for the location of
the mixed-use building on the subject lot. The subject lot is a through lot with frontage on
both West Grand Avenue and West Ferdinand Street. The proposed location of the main
building door and entryway will be on the lot’s West Grand Avenue frontage and will have
a front setback of zero. The building’s first floor was designed with windows facing the
sidewalk located along West Grand Avenue. The proposed building will have a front
setback of 2 ft.-2 in. from the lot’s West Ferdinand Street frontage.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines “transit friendly development” as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
Jocation near the Wester Avenue Metra train station. The Applicant believes the
development of a vacant lot will improve the subject area for residents and other
commuters traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain approximately 5,900 sq. ft. of
retail/commercial space at grade and forty-eight (48) residential units above. The proposed
building will be supported by thirty-four (34) off-street parking spaces. The Applicant is
seeking administrative approval to permit the off-street parking increase for the residential
units pursuant to the TOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace a vacant lot with a
new mixed-use building, which will provide additional residential housing thereby meeting
market demand. Based on the subject property’s proximity to a designated Metra train line
(Western Avenue station), the Applicant believes the project provides transit options and
otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules
promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an area in need.
